source_questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: We can assume a "spherical cow" when analyzing the motion of a cow's leg.
We can safely assume a cow is a point mass when analyzing its position change in the scale of a mile over a certain time period.
We can never assume the cow is in a vacuum, even when we need to ignore the effect of air resistance.
None of the above is correct.

generated_questions.stem: Which of the following statements about simplifying assumptions in mechanics is most reasonable?

options.text: We can model a hummingbird’s wing as a point mass when predicting the detailed bending motion during a wingbeat.
options.explanation: This confuses whole-body motion modeling with the need for an extended-body model to capture wing deformation.

options.text: We can model a city bus as a point mass when tracking its position change over several kilometers on a map.
options.explanation: Over kilometer-scale travel the bus’s size is negligible compared with the distance, so a point-mass model is appropriate.

options.text: We are never allowed to treat the surroundings as a vacuum, even if we intend to neglect air drag in a calculation.
options.explanation: This is incorrect because “vacuum” is often used as an idealization to ignore air resistance when it is negligible.

options.text: None of the above statements is correct.
options.explanation: Option B is a valid modeling approximation, so “none” is not correct.

generated_questions.stem: Which option has the incorrect unit?

options.text: Power: watt
options.explanation: A watt is correctly the SI unit of power (J/s).

options.text: Momentum: kilogram· meter/second
options.explanation: Momentum correctly has units of kg m/s.

options.text: Pressure: newton/meter
options.explanation: Pressure should be force per area (N/m2), so N/m is dimensionally wrong.

options.text: Electric potential: joule/coulomb
options.explanation: A volt is correctly J/C, so this unit matches electric potential.
